As mentioned by @geraldcombs in !19116, we should probably not convert all dissectors. This is fixing a small issue found while converting, and can be committed independently.
Is that a new syntax control on switch conditions ?

It will be when we switch from `gboolean` to `bool`.

`error: switch condition has boolean value [-Werror,-Wswitch-bool]`

(Well, more like a *semantic* control on switch conditions. According to [the GCC 14 manual section on warning options](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc-14.1.0/gcc/Warning-Options.html), It "[warns] when a `switch` statement has an index of boolean type and the case values are outside the range of a boolean type", and the warning appears to be, at least in GCC 14, enabled by default, given that the manual documents `-Wno-switch-bool` to turn the warning *off*.

Given that a `_Bool`/`bool` is intended only to be `false` or `true`, there's really no reason to use a `switch` statement - an `if` suffices.)
